Your node hands the question to grantFace, which owns the routes and answers. The face keeps the answer in RAM and reuses it. What grantFace still PUSHES by owner command is permission only: the face's contact list, so a member's replies get in.

Not claiming. Consequence of Andy's 'appFaceApp's owner doesn't understand appFaceApp nor grantFace', for the record: the face's route question stops being an app:'appFaceApp' packet that a booted app on the owner node answers. It becomes an ordinary api call, peerPost('api', {grantFace: {route: {host}}}), which the owner node dispatches to grantFace over the pipe without reading it. The reply goes back signed by the owner node. So the FACE itself needs the same consent as any member: a row in the owner's contacts (already true, face-owner.js accepts it) AND a place on grantFace's own list. Tests: no appFaceApp code path runs on the owner node; the face's question reaches grantFace; a face not on grantFace's list gets {} and so 404s everything.
